artists.biography:
The Lemonheads are an American alternative rock band first formed in 1986 by Evan Dando, Ben Deily and Jesse Peretz. Dando has remained the band's only constant member.

Since its formation, recording and touring lineups of the band have included co-founders Deily and Peretz, John Strohm (Blake Babies), Doug Trachten, Corey Loog Brennan, Byron Hoagland (Folks On Fire), Ben Daughtrey (Squirrel Bait), Juliana Hatfield (Blake Babies), Nic Dalton (Godstar, Sneeze, The Plunderers), Dave Ryan, Patrick "Murph" Murphy (Dinosaur Jr), Bill Gibson (Eastern Dark), Mark 'Budola' Newman, Kenny Lyon, Vess Ruhtenberg, Devon Ashley, Karl Alvarez and Bill Stevenson (Descendents), P. David Hazel and various others.

After their initial punk-influenced releases and tours as an independent/"college rock" band in the late '80s, the Lemonheads' popularity with a mass audience grew in 1992 with the major label album It's a Shame about Ray, which was produced, engineered, and mixed by The Robb Brothers (Bruce Robb, Dee, and Joe). This was followed by a cover of Simon and Garfunkel's "Mrs. Robinson", which eventually became one of the band's most successful singles. The Lemonheads were active until 1997 before going on hiatus, but reformed with a new lineup in 2005 and released The Lemonheads the following year. The band released its latest album, Varshons, in June 2009.

perplexity.description:
Varshons II is the tenth studio album by American rock band The Lemonheads, released on February 8, 2019, through Fire Records. Following up their 2009 covers album Varshons, this record continues the band’s tradition of reinterpreting songs from a diverse range of artists, blending elements of rock and pop with their signature laid-back, melodic style. The album features covers of tracks by Yo La Tengo, The Eagles, John Prine, Lucinda Williams, Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds, and others, showcasing the band’s ability to put their own spin on material spanning indie rock, country, and alternative genres.

Musically, Varshons II is marked by Evan Dando’s distinctive vocals and the band’s polished yet relaxed arrangements, which balance reverence for the originals with subtle stylistic updates. The album stands as a sequel to their earlier covers project, highlighting The Lemonheads’ enduring affinity for songcraft and their roots in the American indie rock scene. Upon release, Varshons II received mixed reviews, earning a Metacritic score of 68/100, and charted modestly, reaching the UK Independent Albums chart and the US Independent Albums chart. While not a major commercial breakthrough, it reaffirmed the band’s place as respected interpreters within the rock and pop landscape.
